newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity group want more clarity from Offer.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity group want more clarity from Offer.

text.p: A British electricity industry lobby group called on Tuesday for greater accountability and transparency from the regulator Offer but added that current inflation-related price controls were the most effective option.

In the Electricity Industry Review published by the Electricity Association, president David Jefferies said "while greater accountability and transparency is desirable, the RPI-X mechanism is still considered to be the most effective formula."
Electricity price controls are set by industry watchdog Offer and are linked to inflation, or RPI.

Jeffries added the industry continued to support a regulator specifically dedicated to the industry and would not want to see a single energy regulator. The review is published annually and gives a snapshot guide to issues in the industry along with statistics and background. Main opposition Labour party spokesman on energy John Battle, who attended the book's launch, said the review "helps fit together the jigsaw pieces of a rapidly changing electricity market." The report also shows that Britain's electricity prices to large industrial users have fallen as much as 10 percent in cash terms since the over 100 kiloWatt (kW) market opened to competition in 1994.
The review added that domestic electricity prices have come down 11 percent since 1990, when the sector was privatised.

"We are proud of the achievements set out in this review and delighted that the performance of our member companies has...provided so much good news," said Electricity Association chief executive Philip Daubeney.
The association is the trade body for Britain's electricity industry and its main role is to promote the policies of members with government and regulatory bodies.

Battle said Labour, ahead of the ruling Conservatives in polls with a general election to be held by May, "looks forward to working with the Electricity Association...for the speedy completion of a European single market in energy, providing new opportunities and jobs for this industry."
The report is available from the Business Information Centre, the Electricity Association, 30 Millbank, London SW1P 4RD at a cost of 25 stg.
